what_its_for: This combination medicine is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension). Telmisartan relaxes and widens your blood vessels so your heart does not have to work as hard. Hydrochlorothiazide is a 'water pill' (diuretic) that helps your kidneys remove extra salt and water from your body, which also lowers blood pressure. Controlling high blood pressure helps prevent strokes, heart attacks, and kidney problems.
how_to_take: Take this medicine by mouth once a day, with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Try to take it at the same time every day so you do not forget. Do not crush, cut, or chew the tablet. Even if you feel well, keep taking this medicine because high blood pressure often has no symptoms. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor first.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your blood pressure and how well your kidneys are working. Common starting doses are telmisartan 40 mg / hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg once daily. Your doctor may increase your dose if needed, up to a maximum of telmisartan 160 mg / hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg once daily. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. If it is already the next day, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Never take two doses in one day to make up for a missed one, as this can cause your blood pressure to drop too low.
storage: Store at room temperature between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep the tablets in their original packaging and protect them from moisture and heat. Do not store in the bathroom or near the kitchen sink. Keep this medicine out of sight and reach of children and pets. Do not use it after the expiration date printed on the package. Ask your pharmacist how to safely dispose of unused medicine.
what_to_avoid: Avoid potassium supplements, salt substitutes containing potassium, or high-potassium foods (such as large amounts of bananas or orange juice) unless your doctor tells you otherwise, as this medicine can sometimes affect potassium levels. Avoid alcohol, as it can lower your blood pressure further and cause dizziness. Avoid getting up too quickly from a sitting or lying position, as this can cause dizziness or fainting. Limit time in the sun and use sunscreen, since the hydrochlorothiazide in this medicine can make your skin more sensitive to sunlight. Avoid NSAIDs (pain relievers like ibuprofen or naproxen) unless approved by your doctor, as they can reduce how well this medicine works and may harm your kidneys.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat (this could be a serious allergic reaction called angioedema); severe dizziness, fainting, or feeling very lightheaded; little or no urination or signs of kidney problems; muscle cramps, weakness, or irregular heartbeat (signs of low potassium or electrolyte problems); signs of dehydration such as extreme thirst, dry mouth, or very dark urine; severe skin rash or blistering; or if you become pregnant while taking this medicine. Also tell your doctor if your blood pressure is not improving or if you have any new or worsening symptoms.
when_it_works: You may start to see your blood pressure begin to lower within the first 1 to 2 weeks of taking this medicine. However, it may take up to 4 weeks to see the full benefit. Even after your blood pressure is under control, continue taking this medicine every day as directed. Blood pressure control is an ongoing process, and stopping the medicine can cause your blood pressure to rise again.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Do NOT take this medicine if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. It can cause serious harm or death to an unborn baby, especially after the first 3 months of pregnancy. Use effective birth control while taking this medicine and tell your doctor immediately if you become pregnant. Breastfeeding: This medicine may pass into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. Elderly patients: Older adults may be more sensitive to the blood-pressure-lowering effects and may be at higher risk of dizziness and falls. Use caution when standing up quickly. Kidney or liver problems: Your doctor may need to adjust your dose or choose a different medicine if you have severe kidney or liver disease. Children: This medicine is generally not recommended for children. Diabetic patients: Hydrochlorothiazide can raise blood sugar levels. Monitor your blood sugar closely and tell your doctor if you notice changes.
